feat-convert-insightsbookingservice-to-u.text: Keeping nit. The memoization the deleted tests covered is unchanged by the PR apart from the type: insightsBooking.ts:84-86 `if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined) { this.cachedAuthConditions = await this.buildAuthorizationConditions(); }` is the same sentinel the base had; only the annotation went from WhereInput to Prisma.Sql. The PR deleted a test block for trivial, untouched memoization while rewriting the file's expectations; no behaviour the PR introduces goes unverified, and the getBaseConditions/filter tests still exercise both getters. That is test tidying with lost coverage, not a test that fails to verify the change.

Conceding the class. The PR removed findMany (the encapsulated consumer) and made getBaseConditions the public fragment API, but it parenthesizes only the combined case: insightsBooking.ts:73 `(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` vs :75 `return authConditions;`, and org/team auth is a top-level OR (:173, :206 `(${acc}) OR (${condition})`). Any caller composing `WHERE ${base} AND ...` leaks the first OR branch, so the returned contract is unsafe even if no caller composes it yet. Severity high rather than critical: it needs a caller to append a predicate, a security weakness under specific conditions.

feat-ecosystem-implement-cross-system-is.text: Conceding. The loop the comment relies on cannot happen: sync_status_inbound.py:220/:247 call Group.objects.update_group_status, which only bulk_updates and creates activity (group.py ~461-470); outbound status syncs are kicked off only from api/helpers/group_index/update.py:577 and event_manager.py:1807 (kick_off_status_syncs), never from the inbound webhook path. The unused assignment_source parameter on the abstract method is real but the issue's stated problem is false.

implement-recovery-key-support-for-user-.text: Conceding. The null myUser state is not reachable in this test provider: users are only produced by getUserById/getUserByUsername after `if (!users.containsKey(translateUserName(username))) return null;` (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:89, :349), and addUser puts the entry first (:361). Other pre-existing methods dereference the same lookup unguarded (:162, :190, :200). The suggested null check is a guard for an unreachable state.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.text: Keeping FP hallucination. The comment's mechanism is false: the search reader does not consume the broadcaster's events; each caller gets its own poller and channel (sql/backend.go:558-567 `stream := make(chan *resource.WrittenEvent); go b.poller(ctx, since, stream)`), so search.go:203 and server.go:755 are independent streams. And no Watch subscriber can exist in the window: Init now runs inside NewResourceServer (server.go:258 `err := s.Init(ctx)`) before the server is returned. Events before the broadcaster starts were never replayable to Watch even with the old order (Watch only filters the live broadcaster stream, server.go:847-867), so the reorder creates no new loss for any subscriber.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.text: Keeping nit. The client cache is intentional: create_account_controller.js:275 pushes only server-rejected emails (`if (result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values)`), and :69 short-circuits them so the user is not sent to resubmit a known-bad address. It only goes stale if an admin lifts the BlockedEmail rule during the same page session, and a reload clears it. Real but a corner-case UX staleness, not a defect a reviewer would block on.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.text: Conceding. Rechecked the evaluator: for the all-groups type resource (owner = resource server) DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:76 skips the typed-resource loop, and the scope lookup is findByScopes(server, null, ...) which uses findPolicyIdByNullResourceScope (`pe.resources is empty`), so other group resources' permissions are never pulled in. DecisionPermissionCollector.grantPermission builds every Permission from permission.getResource(), so returned permissions always carry the evaluated resource's id; the UserPermissionsV2 filter is a no-op there, and the claimed cross-resource grant cannot occur. Severity as stated (permission bypass) is critical.

Conceding. The per-group check is deliberate: GroupPermissionsV2.java:141-150 evaluates the group's own resource when one exists and falls back to all-groups only otherwise, so a global VIEW grant cannot answer for every group, and hoisting canView() would bypass group-specific permissions. Admins with VIEW/MANAGE_USERS short-circuit at :56-58. Correct, intended behaviour; the proposed fix would be wrong.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.text: Conceding the subclass. The facts in the comment are true (organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 reads attendees[0] unchecked), but the empty state is unreachable: addGuests.handler.ts:80-81 throws on empty uniqueGuests and the event is built from the updated attendees (:92-136). Per the rubric, a guard for a state no code path can reach is FP with no subclass, not a hallucination.
